title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

McKinsey’s September 2026 analysis argues that artificial intelligence is changing both the size of the semiconductor market and where its profits are made. After an exceptional surge in chip sales, the firm raised its 2030 base-case market forecast to $2.3 trillion, up from the $1.6 trillion it projected in autumn 2025. Its current scenarios range from $1.7 trillion to $2.6 trillion. These figures are forecasts, shaped by assumptions about AI investment, supply and chip prices.

Data centers drive much of the revision. McKinsey expects semiconductor revenue from servers and data centers to climb from $330 billion in 2025 to $1.2 trillion in 2030. Demand is increasing for leading-edge processors and memory, particularly high-bandwidth memory, which helps keep AI computing hardware supplied with data. Manufacturing capacity is constrained, so McKinsey expects both sales volumes and average prices to rise in these segments. That combination differs from the industry’s familiar pattern of falling prices as production expands.

The gains will be uneven. McKinsey estimates that leading-edge chips could add $710 billion in market value by 2030 and memory another $560 billion. Older manufacturing nodes will still supply components for connectivity, power systems and other applications, but their overall growth is expected to be smaller, with prices declining even as volumes rise. McKinsey

The $2.3 trillion outcome is far from guaranteed. It depends on sustained data-center funding, measurable returns from AI, affordable power, lower costs for running AI models and a stable economy. A recession, trade disruption or disappointing AI returns could weaken investment. McKinsey’s central message is therefore both an opportunity and a planning challenge: chipmakers should prepare for a much larger market while testing their investments against several possible outcomes.

Source: McKinsey
